label: Searched — Awaiting Classification
help: The search finished under an older result format that cannot be assigned one of the newer screening classes.

label: No Transit Detected in Search Window
help: No repeating transit-like signal reached the automated threshold in the searched TESS window. This does not prove the star has no planet.

label: Strongest Signal Screened Out
help: The strongest repeating signal failed one or more automated plausibility checks. The rejection applies to that signal, not to every possible planet around the star.

label: Single-Event Lead — Longer Baseline Needed
help: One promising dimming event was present, but the observed time span was not long enough to establish a repeating orbit. Longer-baseline data should be checked.

label: Automated Survivor — Deeper Vetting Needed
help: A signal survived the automated gates and has been placed in the deeper follow-up queue. It is not yet a vetted candidate or discovery.

label: Search Error — Retry Needed
help: This target did not finish successfully because data retrieval or analysis failed. It needs a retry and is not counted as a no-signal result.

label: Mapped Planet Recovery
help: The search recovered a planet that was already known. This checks the pipeline; it is not a new discovery.

label: TCE Rediscovery
help: The signal matches an existing TESS threshold-crossing event, so TESS has already flagged it.

label: Known Eclipsing-Binary Rediscovery
help: The TIC host and recovered period match an authoritative eclipsing-binary record. This is useful validation and possible eclipse-timing material, but it is not a planet survivor.

label: Known Binary Host — Residual Review
help: The star is a known binary, but the recovered period is not yet tied to its catalogued eclipse. The binary must be modeled before a separate residual or circumbinary interpretation is considered.

label: Known Variable Star — Signal Review
help: Gaia or SIMBAD records stellar variability that can imitate transit-like dips. This signal remains in a stellar-variability review lane.

label: Crowding / Contamination Review
help: Nearby sources can contribute flux inside a TESS pixel. Difference imaging or target-pixel localization is required before this lead can advance.

label: Public-Catalog Coverage Gap
help: One or more applicable public catalogs do not yet cover the searched sector or signal. Independent data checks are still required.

label: Context Checks Incomplete — Retry Needed
help: At least one authoritative metadata source failed. The context pass must be retried; absence from the sources that did respond is not meaningful clearance.

label: Unresolved Transit-Like Signal
help: No checked catalog currently explains the signal. It is still only an unresolved lead and must pass pixel localization, independent reduction, repeat-epoch, and human false-positive review.

label: Lost Light Localized Off Target
help: Difference imaging places the lost light more than one TESS pixel from this star, so the dimming most likely belongs to a neighbouring source rather than the target. The centroid is a screening measurement; one pixel spans roughly 21 arcseconds.

label: On Target — Single Supporting Sector
help: The light was lost on target, but only the discovery sector supports the fixed ephemeris. A signal absent from independently searched sectors is not yet coherent; it may still be a systematic, or the other sectors may not constrain it well.

label: On Target and Multi-Sector Coherent
help: The lost light is on target and the fixed ephemeris is supported in more than one independently searched sector. This is the strongest screening state this pipeline produces and is still not a planet candidate: independent reduction, alias checks, and human review remain outstanding.

label: Observatory Systematic — Shared Ephemeris
help: Many unrelated stars observed at the same time carry this exact ephemeris, far more than chance allows, and they span multiple cameras and a wide area of sky. A transit belongs to one star; a signal shared this widely was produced by the observatory — scattered light, a momentum dump, or a detrending artifact at a downlink gap. Multi-sector coherence cannot clear this, because such an event repeats identically in every sector.

label: Shared Ephemeris With Close Neighbours
help: This ephemeris is shared by an improbable number of nearby targets confined to a small area of sky. That pattern points to one bright variable or eclipsing source bleeding into the apertures of its neighbours rather than an observatory-wide effect.

label: Search Artifact — Fit Sits On An Instrument Or Grid Rail
help: The fit lands on a spacecraft harmonic, on the first or last value of the duration grid, or at the search ceiling. None of these is a property of the star: they are places a fit goes when it is describing a trend, a momentum dump, or the edge of the search rather than a transit. Measured across 84,374 screened targets these three flags are enriched 1.60x, 2.86x and 2.35x among automated survivors and together account for 311 of 1,010 of them, against 14.8% of the screened population. Unlike the shared-ephemeris screen this is a single-star verdict and needs no neighbours to establish.

label: Vetted False Positive
help: Follow-up checks indicate that the signal is probably not a transiting planet.

label: Vetted New Candidate
help: A promising signal has passed the current checks, but it is still not a confirmed planet.

label: Confirmed Planet
help: Independent evidence has established this object as a planet.

label: Review Packet Assembled
help: Every automated check this pipeline can run has been run and its evidence collected into one packet: ephemeris and fit posteriors, T3 gate values, population screen, catalog adjudication with the snapshot hashes it was decided against, pixel localization, the multi-reduction depth table, completeness at this period and depth, and the full provenance chain. This is the strongest state the system may assign on its own. It is not a candidate and not a detection: calling it either requires a human, and calling it a validated planet requires evidence this pipeline cannot produce.
